description: URLs already on the legacy CMS CDN — rehost as-is, no path rewriting
reasoning: Found while planning: a large share of URLs in the exports (mostly videos and auto-resized images) are already absolute CDN links. Edge redirect rules never see them because no redirect is involved — but they still depend on the old CMS staying alive, so they need rehosting too. Without this rule they would silently stay behind.

description: Older CDN hostname (portal id already in path) -> current CDN host -> rehost
reasoning: Found while planning: a handful of old blog images use the platform's previous CDN domain, with the portal id already present in the path. Mapping them through the generic rule below would double the portal id and 404; this rule maps them to the current CDN host correctly.

description: Site-hosted /hs-fs/hubfs/* image URLs -> CDN -> rehost on the new CMS
reasoning: Mirrors edge redirect rule 1 (redirect /hs-fs/hubfs/* image URLs to the CMS CDN) — but instead of redirecting forever, the file is downloaded from the CDN and rehosted on the new CMS so the redirect becomes unnecessary.

description: Site-hosted /hubfs/* asset and PDF URLs -> CDN -> rehost on the new CMS
reasoning: Mirrors edge redirect rule 2 (redirect /hubfs/* asset and PDF URLs to the CMS CDN) — rehosted on the new CMS instead of redirected, same as rule site-hosted-images.

description: Third-party files on someone else's instance of the same CMS — rehost from their own host
reasoning: Found while checking: some assets referenced in content are hosted on a partner's portal, not ours. The generic rule above wrongly mapped them onto our CDN, where they 404. This rule downloads such files from their own host instead. Ordered after the site rules so it only catches foreign hosts.

description: A legacy-host path with no equivalent on the new site — points at the docs site instead
reasoning: The generic legacy-host rewrite below produced a path that 404s on the primary domain (that section never moved). A human chose the docs-site article as the replacement target. Every orphan like this needs a decision — the tool surfaces them, it does not guess.

description: A legacy-host path that was renamed on the new site
reasoning: The generic rewrite produced /partners, which 404s on the primary domain. A human chose /integrations as the replacement target.

description: legacy.example.com/* -> same path, query preserved; host '' = relative link
reasoning: Mirrors edge redirect rule 3 (redirect legacy.example.com/* to the same path on the primary domain, preserving the query string). Rewritten as relative links so the new CMS's own redirects handle moved pages and the content survives any future domain change. Set host to an absolute URL to change that.
